📍 DOUBLE KNOT — PHL @doubleknot_phl 
This felt like a Japanese tapas style happy hour spot! You are supposed to order a few small plates to share. The dim lighting, ambience, and attentive staff made it very comfortable and cozy. We stayed here for about 1 1/2 hours and ordered 4 dishes and 2 rounds of drinks. 

Food:
Maitake mushroom (8/10): it was smoky and buttery with a soy sauce flavor
Shrimp tempura roll (7/10): this was a standard shrimp tempura roll— crispy and fresh
Kim chee fried rice (10/10): this was my fav dish! It was spicy, savory, and super satisfying + the poached egg on top added a nice texture 
Japanese fried chicken (7/10): crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside

Drinks:
Sake (8/10): My first time trying sake! It was easy and smooth
The tautline hitch (10/10): My fav drink! It was a gingery vodka cocktail with lime
The sheet bend (8/10): this was a tequila cocktail with cherry lime vibes

Overall, the portions + quality for happy hour were 🔥. Vibe is cozy, dim, and perfect for a chill night out in Philly. Definitely coming back!!

had to try this popular vegan sushi spot in Philly and it didn’t disappoint! In order of ranking, we got:

1.  Veggie on Fire: cucumber, avocado, fried onion, topped with spicy zucchini sauce

2. Vegan Tomo: spicy vegan tuna (watermelon), avocado, cilantro, topped with seared vegan tuna

3. Vegan Green Dragon: spicy vegan tuna, avocado, topped with vegan eel (eggplant) & unagi sauce

4. Vegan Harvest: Shiitake, avocado, shibazuke, topped with sweet potatoes, fried onions & coconut flakes

5. Vegan Cheesesteak: braised steak (seitan), cucumber, oshinko, topped with Chao cheese & fried onions

6. Vegan Chao: shiitake, vegan cream cheese, avocado, topped with seared vegan chao cheese

Sushi has never been a go-to meal for me as a vegetarian bc there aren’t too many options so I was excited to see how vegan sushi compares. Each roll had a unique flavor profile and it allowed me to try flavors I wouldn’t have been able to before!! 

I would say a must try for vegetarians and sushi lovers!!

I tried their 15 course omakase menu (only $78) and we got to watch the chef hand make each roll fresh! It was like having a show and a meal in one. I also thought that eel was surprisingly delicious. I’ve had eel at other places, and they did not taste nearly as good as this one. This one almost tasted barbecued! Plus they torched the outside to give it a nice charred flavor! The cocktails were light and refreshing but they have a great selection of sake flights and bottles to choose from as well. You can tell that the fish and ingredients in general are fresh! Definitely check them out!🍣✨

Took my wife to @sullivanssteakhouse last night for Valentine’s Day. This was the first time we’ve eaten here. Overall, it was a good experience. The ambiance was amazing and the staff were great. We were early for our reservation and we were seated early, which was nice. 

My wife ordered a Valentine’s special drink called a love bug and she loved it. It had a raspberry and chocolate flavor that was delicious. We ordered the Cheesesteak egg rolls as an appetizer and they were tasty, but will probably try something different next time. 

We both ordered the ribeye based on a recommendation and it was pretty good. I had mine prepared medium rare and my wife’s was medium. Both were cooked perfectly. It was not as tender as I’ve had at other places. That was disappointing. We ordered three sides, wild mushrooms, lobster garlic mashed potatoes, and the sweet potato casserole. The mushrooms were fantastic! We should have ordered the mashed potatoes without the lobster as we didn’t really love that combination. The sweet potato casserole was the highlight of the meal, which shouldn’t have been at a steakhouse. It was so delicious!!

When we received our bill, they brought two complimentary chocolate covered strawberries. They were wonderful!

We’ll give it another go, of course, but might try the filet next time. Based on the positives, we’d recommend Sullivan’s to others.
